item.description:
Unison UI for macOS 0.8.0

Version 0.8.0 changes how the app's unison command reaches your PATH and adds a guided check that a remote sync profile will use the Unison you intend on the far side. The command is now placed on your PATH by editing your own login-shell startup file, with your consent and without an administrator password; the 0.7.0 installer that wrote a link under /usr/local/bin is removed. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration.

Added

  • Guided remote check. Before you depend on an ssh profile, get a read on what the far side will run: a version or engine mismatch on the remote is a common cause of sync failures, and it is easier to look up front than mid-sync. The check tests whether this profile's remote command reports a Unison version over ssh, and offers discovered alternatives if you want to change it. Discovery uses a plain sh lookup, which may resolve commands differently from the profile. Only a synchronization confirms the server protocol. It changes nothing on either side, is reachable from the profile picker and the Profile Editor, states the current result first, titles its alternatives by their consequence, and reports a failed connection plainly. Effective-value fields show the actual host, user, port, and remote command a profile will use; the advice that avoids the question is an absolute servercmd in the peer's profile, which the pane can copy and the check can assess.
  • Command-line setup through your login shell (Settings ▸ Command Line). So you can type unison and get this app — unison -ui graphic opens it, and the same install serves Unison's text interface and its ssh-server role — the app can put its command on your PATH. Its command lives inside the bundle at Contents/SharedSupport/bin/unison. Add Terminal Setup puts that directory on your PATH by writing a marked, app-managed block to your own shell startup file — automatically only when the case is unambiguous and safe (a recognized stock zsh startup, this app's own earlier block, or a stated set of bash and fish cases), and otherwise as Manual setup, where the pane shows what to add and names the file to edit when it can identify one — when it cannot safely identify the file, such as a redirected ZDOTDIR or an unsupported shell, it says so rather than point at the wrong file. The pane leads with what unison resolves to in your login shell and names it — this app, another copy, no unison, could not be checked, or manual — with the resolved path shown as evidence, and offers Use This Copy, Remove Terminal Setup, and copying the app's command path. Removing restores the file with its other contents intact. No administrator password, and nothing is written outside your own files. macOS 15 and macOS 26 stock /etc/zprofile are recognized so a fresh account is offered automatic zsh setup; an unrecognized system file falls back to Manual setup rather than guessing.
  • Profile Editor keyboard navigation. The General, Roots, File Attributes, Options, and Includes sections of the Profile Editor are navigable from the keyboard.

Changed

  • Homebrew cask is unison-ui. Homebrew's token rules drop platform suffixes, so the tap's cask is bcourbage/tap/unison-ui; installs under the old token migrate on their own at the next brew update, and Settings ▸ Command Line recognizes a Homebrew-managed install under either token.

Removed

  • The 0.7.0 privileged command installer and its administrator prompt. The unison command is now placed on your PATH through your own login-shell startup file (Settings ▸ Command Line). A /usr/local/bin/unison link left by 0.7.0 keeps working — it points at the app's launcher, and Settings reports it as this app — and is not removed automatically; remove it yourself if you no longer want it.

Compatibility

  • No profile or settings migration is required. Same system requirements as 0.7.0: macOS 15 or later, Apple Silicon.
  • Automatic updates are delivered through Sparkle; Homebrew users update with brew upgrade --cask unison-ui.

Unison UI for macOS 0.7.0

Version 0.7.0 adds a unison command to the app. One install now serves both the graphical interface and Unison's command-line roles, including acting as the far side of an SSH profile, so a Mac with this app no longer needs a separate Unison installation. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration.

Added

  • The unison command. The app bundle carries a command-line launcher. Once linked onto your PATH under the name unison, it behaves like Unison's own command: unison -ui graphic opens this app, unison <profile> and unison -ui text <profile> run Unison's text interface in the terminal on the app's embedded engine, and unison -server, which another machine runs over ssh when it syncs to this Mac, is served by the app's engine headlessly. Arguments reach Unison exactly as typed, so everything Unison accepts on the command line works the same way here. A profile named after -ui graphic is preselected in the profile picker.
  • Settings ▸ Command Line. Shows what unison currently resolves to on two PATHs, the one a login shell builds and the one macOS gives commands arriving over ssh, and names it: this app's command, another copy of this app, the Homebrew unison formula, upstream Unison.app, a broken link, or something else. One button is offered only when the evidence supports it: Install when nothing owns the name, Repair when a broken link points at a former copy of this app, Remove for this installation's own link. Each asks for an administrator password, and each re-checks the link at the moment it runs.
  • First-launch offer. When nothing on either PATH is named unison, or a broken link points at a former copy of this app, the app offers to install or repair the command once per launch after the profile picker appears. "Not Now" asks again next time; "Do not ask again" stops the offer, and the Settings tab remains the way to install later.

Compatibility

  • No profile or settings migration is required. Same system requirements as 0.6.1: macOS 15 or later, Apple Silicon.
  • Installing the command writes one link at /usr/local/bin/unison. Homebrew users get the link from the cask instead, under the Homebrew prefix, once the cask for this version is published. Only one command can hold the name: if the Homebrew unison formula is linked, either unlink it or keep it and install the app from the zip without the command.
  • Machines that sync to this Mac over ssh run unison -server here in a non-interactive shell. /usr/local/bin is on that shell's PATH on a stock macOS; the Homebrew prefix is not, so peers of a Homebrew install should set servercmd in their profile. Launch the app once from Finder before relying on it as an ssh peer, so macOS completes its first-open check of the download.
  • If automatic update checking is enabled, Sparkle notifies you when 0.7.0 is available. You can also update any time from App menu ▸ Check for Updates.

Unison UI for macOS 0.6.1

Version 0.6.1 is a small user-interface and update-infrastructure release on top of 0.6.0. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration.

Fixed

  • The reconcile toolbar no longer shifts between phases. After a scan finished, the Go button used to move to where another control had been, because a single button was relabelled and resized per phase. The toolbar is now spatially stable: every button keeps its position, so Go stays where you expect it.

Changed

  • Stop is a sync-only control. The Stop button keeps its "Stop" label and its position in every phase, and is active (red) only while a synchronization is running, when it aborts that sync. During a connect or scan it is inactive. To return to the profile list at any time, including during a scan, use Profiles (or ⌘⇧P). Leaving during a scan does not cancel it; the scan continues in the background. If it does not finish, quit and relaunch the app. Rescan is disabled while a scan or sync is already running.
  • Update checks now go through updates.courbage.net. Builds from 0.6.1 onward check for updates through a project-run proxy rather than contacting GitHub Pages directly. It serves the same signed appcast byte-for-byte, so update integrity is unchanged and a signed feed is still required.

When anonymous system-profile sharing is enabled, the project records a bounded per-check telemetry row containing the shared profile fields and coarse country, subject to the documented retention period. When sharing is disabled, the project creates no telemetry record, although Cloudflare still processes the request as the hosting provider. No IP address, user agent, cookie, or user identifier is stored. See what data the app sends in the FAQ.

Compatibility

  • No profile or settings migration is required. Same system requirements as 0.6.0: macOS 15 or later, Apple Silicon.
  • The move to updates.courbage.net takes effect for update checks made by this build and later. A 0.6.0 install discovers 0.6.1 through its existing feed; once 0.6.1 is installed, its later checks use the new address.
  • If automatic update checking is enabled, Sparkle notifies you when 0.6.1 is available; whether it then downloads and installs automatically or only after you confirm depends on the separate automatic-download choice from the first-launch prompt. You can also update any time from App menu ▸ Check for Updates.
